children: NVIDIA reportedly approached Arm CEO Rene Haas as a possible successor to Jensen Huang. The board said it had not formally contacted candidates and was still choosing an executive search firm.
NVIDIA (NVDA) was set to report fiscal third-quarter results after market close November 17. It forecast revenue of $108 billion, +/-2%; analysts expected $109.2 billion and adjusted EPS of $2.48.
NVIDIA shares opened at $151, down from the prior close of $173.73, after a resignation announcement. They fell as much as 14% intraday and closed about 4% lower.
Trump administration officials, including Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick and Scott Bessent, reportedly disagree over limits on NVIDIA chip exports to China.
NVIDIA’s quarter ended October 25, before its leadership change. Guidance for the next quarter was set to be the first issued with CFO Colette Kress as interim CEO.
A petition urging NVIDIA’s board to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO during an independent investigation surpassed 135,000 signatures Sunday. Signers’ affiliations have not been independently verified.
NVIDIA customers say its chips remain their preferred choice despite expected near-term shortages and leadership uncertainty, though some are considering AI servers from rival suppliers.
Yorkville Ives lowered its price target for NVIDIA Corporation (NVDA) to $225 from $300 and maintained a buy rating. NVIDIA Corporation (NVDA) shares ended the week at $162.85.
President Donald Trump said he had spoken with Huang and later suggested former Apple CEO Tim Cook as Huang’s replacement at NVIDIA Corporation (NVDA).
- NVIDIA Corporation (NVDA) reportedly decided to let Huang go; Lex Fridman criticized the decision as a major mistake and praised Huang’s character.
